channel.title: Hindu Research Portal — Research News
channel.description: Latest research, archaeology, manuscripts, heritage and cultural news from Hindu Research Portal.

item.title: Ancient Indian Inscriptions Uncovered in Egypt's Valley of the Kings
item.description: Archaeologists have discovered nearly 30 inscriptions in ancient Indian languages within six tombs in the Valley of the Kings, shedding new light on Indian presence in Ancient Egypt. The majority of these inscriptions are in Tamil-Brahmi, an ancient language connected to modern Tamil. This finding suggests a significant integration of Indians into Roman Egyptian society between the first and third centuries AD.

item.title: Unveiling India's Epigraphical Heritage: A Window into the Past
item.description: The Archaeological Survey of India's Epigraphy Branch has been instrumental in uncovering the country's rich epigraphical wealth, with over one lakh inscriptions discovered to date. These inscriptions provide valuable insights into India's history and culture, spanning from the Mauryan period to the late medieval era. The branch, established in 1886, has been collecting, editing, and publishing inscriptions, shedding light on the country's past.

item.title: Deciphering Indus Script Inscriptions: Unveiling Ancient India's Cultural History
item.description: Research on Indian inscriptions has shed light on the cultural and artistic history of ancient India, with a focus on deciphering the Indus Script and its connection to Hindu iconography. The study of epigraphic evidence has revealed the significance of inscriptions in understanding religious practices and societal dynamics. This area of research has the potential to reconstruct historical narratives about ancient and medieval India

item.title: Unveiling India's Rich History: The National Archives of India
item.description: The National Archives of India serves as the primary custodian of the government's enduring records, established in 1891 in Calcutta. It houses a vast collection of records, including public and private papers, oriental records, and microfilms. This repository offers invaluable sources for researching Indian history and culture

item.title: Unveiling the Significance of a Newly Discovered Sanskrit Manuscript in Mahāyāna Sūtras
item.description: A recently published Sanskrit manuscript of the Jayamatiparipṛcchāsūtra has been found to have a previously unrecognized relationship with the Śūraṃgama-samādhisūtra, both of which are classified as Mahāyāna sūtras. The manuscript provides new insights into the content and context of these texts, and its publication is a significant contribution to the study of Indian scriptural materials. The article offers suggestions for improvement to the edited texts and presents a comparative analysis of the original Sanskrit and Tibetan translations.

item.title: Exploring Mimamsa: A School of Indian Philosophy
item.description: Mimamsa is a significant school of Indian philosophy, with a rich bibliography of academic papers and books available for research. The PhilPapers database provides a comprehensive list of publications on Mimamsa, including works by notable authors such as Madan Mohan Agrawal and Daya Krishna. These publications cover various aspects of Mimamsa philosophy, including its relation to other Indian philosophical systems like Nyaya and Vedanta.

item.title: Unpacking the Gurukul System: Holistic Education in Ancient India
item.description: The Gurukul system was a traditional Indian educational model that emphasized holistic development through a residential teacher-disciple relationship, focusing on self-discipline, ethical values, and critical thinking. This system aimed to integrate spiritual, moral, intellectual, and physical growth in students. The Gurukul model has its roots in classical teachings and has evolved to incorporate contemporary methodologies

item.title: Unveiling Ancient India's History through Epigraphs and Inscriptions
item.description: The Archaeological Survey of India has digitized over 67,000 estampages of Indian epigraphs, shedding light on the country's ancient history. Epigraphs are a valuable source of information on social, political, economic, and cultural aspects of ancient Indian society. The study of inscriptions, such as the Naneghat Cave inscription, has provided significant insights into the past

item.title: National Archives of India Achieves 60% Digitization of Archival Records
item.description: The National Archives of India has made significant progress in digitizing its vast collection of historical documents, with over 20 crore pages now available online. This effort aims to preserve India's rich cultural heritage and provide access to valuable historical records. The digitized collection includes notable documents such as the Mountbatten plan papers and manuscripts of prominent Indian figures.

item.title: Sanskrit Manuscript Critical Edition: Table of Contents Revealed
item.description: A scholarly publication of a Sanskrit manuscript has been released, featuring a critical edition and diplomatic edition of the text. The manuscript is analyzed in detail, including its description, relationships, and stemma. The publication also includes a preface, general introduction, and introduction to the critical edition.

item.title: Unpacking the Evolution of Nyāya's Philosophy of Language in Premodern South Asia
item.description: A doctoral research project at Cornell University is exploring the intellectual history of Gaṅgeśa's philosophy of language in the Tattvacintāmaṇi, a 14th-century text. The study delves into the reconfiguration of linguistic theories by Śālikanātha, a key figure in the Prābhākāra Mīmāṃsā tradition. This research sheds light on the development of Nyāya's philosophy of language in premodern South Asia

item.title: Science & Medicine | The Story of India - Photo Gallery | PBS
item.description: Astronomy, astrology, mathematics, and religion were closely linked in ancient India. Astronomy developed out of the need to determine solstices, equinoxes, and phases of the moon for Vedic rituals. item.title: Deciphering Ancient Shaivite Traditions: 5th Century Sanskrit Seal Uncovered
item.description: The Archaeological Survey of India has successfully decoded a 5th century Sanskrit seal, shedding new light on ancient Shaivite traditions and the existence of a Shaiva temple in the mythical Deodarvana. The seal, discovered in present-day Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, features a rare Sanskrit inscription written in Brahmi script. This discovery contributes to a deeper understanding of India's cultural and religious heritage

item.title: Unlocking India's Archival Treasures: National Archives of India's Digital Initiatives
item.description: The National Archives of India has made significant strides in digitizing its vast repository of records, including declassified files relating to Netaji, to facilitate research and public access. The archives' online portal, Abhilekh Patal, provides a comprehensive search platform for scholars and users. The National Archives of India is the largest archival repository in South Asia, housing a diverse range of records and materials

item.title: Comprehensive Encyclopedia of Hinduism Covers Diverse Aspects of the Tradition
item.description: A new encyclopedia on Hinduism provides an in-depth look at various aspects of the tradition, including art, history, language, and literature. The encyclopedia aims to offer a better understanding of Hinduism in a global context. It covers topics such as Hinduism in different regions and its development in Hindu kingdoms and empires.
